note: a name that STARTS with what you typed does not come above a name that merely contains it further along - the two score exactly the same, so the stronger match gets no advantage at all. The third part of the check is fine: the typo-only match scores far lower and comes last, correctly marked as a close match.
evidence:
Reported and now raised: SV-10211 - https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10211 - raised on 17 September 2026 against the ranking work, with the annotated picture and the requirement quoted.

WITH THE DATA SOUND, typing ZZPREFIX and opening the Customers tab gives three customers in this order:
  1. Bolton ZZPREFIX Services  - the words appear part-way through the name
  2. ZZPREFIX Freight Ltd      - the name STARTS with what was typed
  3. ZZPREFIY Cartage          - reachable only by a typo, shown as a close match

The third line is right. The first two are the wrong way round.

THE PRODUCT'S OWN NUMBERS SHOW WHY, read straight from it:
  Bolton ZZPREFIX Services  - recorded as a whole-word match - score 0.90000004
  ZZPREFIX Freight Ltd      - recorded as a match on the start of the name - score 0.90000004
  ZZPREFIY Cartage          - recorded as a typo match - score 0.45
The product correctly recognises WHICH kind of match each one is, and then gives the first two an identical score. So the stronger kind of match earns nothing, and which of the two comes first is left to chance.

WHAT THE REQUIREMENT ASKS FOR, quoted from the Global Search product requirements page (Confluence 576978945, version 17, read live 17 September 2026, section 6.1): a match on the start of the name is worth +0.70 and a whole-word match anywhere is worth +0.50. They are not meant to be equal.

RULED OUT BEFORE REPORTING: neither customer has any open work orders (both read zero), both carry the same address, the same telephone and no contacts, so no other ranking signal can be lifting the second one. The only difference between them is the kind of name match.

EARLIER TODAY THIS CHECK WAS BLOCKED: the record meant to be reachable only by a typo was also an ordinary match, so the comparison proved nothing. The customer was renamed from ZZPREFIXX Cartage to ZZPREFIY Cartage and the rename was read back before anything was concluded.

What needs to be done: the fix is with the developers on SV-10211; mark this check passed once the stronger match is scored above the weaker one.
